project.name: Royal Restaurant POS
project.description: Android POS system for restaurant management: table ordering, menu management, staff management, payment, and real-time statistics. Connects to a PHP/MySQL backend on Cloud VPS via Retrofit REST API.

nodes.name: build.gradle
nodes.summary: Android module-level Gradle build configuration declaring dependencies (Retrofit, Glide, Material, OkHttp), SDK versions, and build types for the Royal Restaurant POS app.

nodes.name: proguard-rules.pro
nodes.summary: ProGuard/R8 rules file for the Android app, specifying code shrinking and obfuscation settings for the release build.

nodes.name: ExampleInstrumentedTest.java
nodes.summary: Boilerplate Android instrumented test that verifies the application package name against the expected value using InstrumentationRegistry.

nodes.name: AndroidManifest.xml
nodes.summary: Android application manifest declaring all Activity components, permissions (INTERNET, CAMERA, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE), and the entry-point SplashActivity for the Royal Restaurant POS app.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares SplashActivity as the LAUNCHER activity, establishing the app entry point. All Activities must be registered here for Android to recognize them.

nodes.name: AddCategoryActivity.java

nodes.name: AddCategoryActivity
nodes.summary: Activity that allows administrators to add or edit a menu category, including image upload (bitmap resizing and Base64 encoding) and API submission with input validation.

nodes.name: AddMenuActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity for creating and editing menu dishes, including image upload, price formatting with locale-aware number formatting, availability status selection, and API submission.

nodes.name: AddMenuActivity
nodes.summary: Activity for adding or editing menu dishes with image handling, real-time price formatting via TextWatcher, dish status radio group, and Retrofit API calls.

nodes.name: AddStaffActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity for creating and editing staff records with comprehensive field validation (name, username, email, phone, password pattern, gender, role, and age), submitting data via Retrofit.

nodes.name: AddStaffActivity
nodes.summary: Activity for creating or editing staff accounts, featuring 8 validation methods covering all required fields plus password regex validation and a minimum age constraint.

nodes.name: AddTableActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity for adding or renaming dining tables, with name validation and Retrofit API call to create or update a table record.

nodes.name: AddTableActivity

nodes.name: AmountMenuActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity for specifying dish quantity when adding an item to an order, handling order retrieval or creation via API and adding the order detail to the backend.

nodes.name: AmountMenuActivity
nodes.summary: Activity that validates dish quantity, fetches or creates an order for the table, then submits the order detail via Retrofit using SessionManager for staff identity.

nodes.name: CashierConfirmActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity for the cashier to review an order's details and confirm payment via cash or bank transfer, fetching order items and calling the payment confirmation API.

nodes.name: CashierConfirmActivity
nodes.summary: Cashier-role Activity displaying order details in a RecyclerView and providing cash or bank payment confirmation buttons backed by Retrofit API calls.

nodes.name: DetailStatisticActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity for viewing the line-item breakdown of a specific completed order, displaying dish name, quantity, price, and thumbnail in a RecyclerView loaded from the API.

nodes.name: DetailStatisticActivity
nodes.summary: Statistic detail Activity that renders order metadata and a paginated list of ordered items using AdapterDisplayPayment loaded via getOrderDetails API.

nodes.name: HomeActivity.java
nodes.summary: Main application Activity with a Navigation Drawer hosting multiple fragments (Home, Cashier, Statistic, Table, Category, Staff), role-based menu visibility, and periodic session validation that kicks out concurrently-logged-in accounts.

nodes.name: HomeActivity
nodes.summary: Central Activity managing fragment navigation via DrawerLayout, enforcing role-based menu visibility, and running a Handler-based polling loop (startSessionCheck/stopSessionCheck) tied to onResume/onPause lifecycle to implement single-session login.

nodes.name: LoginActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity handling staff login with credentials sent to the backend API, session persistence via SessionManager, and optional Remember Me functionality using Base64-encoded SharedPreferences.

nodes.name: LoginActivity
nodes.summary: Login screen Activity calling the login API endpoint, saving session via SessionManager, and persisting credentials to SharedPreferences with Base64 password encoding for the Remember Me feature.

nodes.name: PaymentActivity.java
nodes.summary: Android Activity managing the full customer payment flow: displaying ordered items, presenting payment method selection dialog (cash or VietQR bank transfer with dynamic QR code), polling for cashier approval, and rendering a shareable receipt dialog on success.

nodes.name: PaymentActivity
nodes.summary: Payment flow Activity with VietQR integration: submits checkout, polls checkOrderStatus at intervals via Handler, stops polling on cashier approval, then renders an inflated receipt dialog with a share-as-image option.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Handler.postDelayed polling pattern for real-time order approval status rather than WebSockets, cleanly stopping on onDestroy via stopPolling.

nodes.name: Register2ndActivity.java
nodes.summary: Second step of the public self-registration flow where new staff provide gender and date of birth, complete validation, and submit the full registration to the API.

nodes.name: Register2ndActivity
nodes.summary: Second-step registration Activity receiving user data via Bundle from RegisterActivity, validating gender and minimum age, and calling addStaff API before redirecting to login.

nodes.name: RegisterActivity.java
nodes.summary: First step of the self-registration flow collecting full name, username, email, phone, and password, validating all fields, then passing data via Bundle to Register2ndActivity.

nodes.name: RegisterActivity
nodes.summary: First registration step Activity with 5 validation methods for name, username, email, phone, and password fields, passing validated data to Register2ndActivity via Bundle.

nodes.name: SplashActivity.java

nodes.name: WelcomeActivity.java
nodes.summary: Landing screen Activity presenting Login and Sign Up buttons with shared element transitions, automatically redirecting to HomeActivity if a valid session already exists.

nodes.name: ApiClient.java
nodes.summary: Singleton Retrofit HTTP client factory that configures OkHttp timeouts (30s), lenient GSON parsing, and exposes the backend base URL plus banking constants (bank ID, account, name) for VietQR integration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a static singleton pattern with lazy initialization; exposes BANK_ID, BANK_ACC, BANK_NAME constants used by PaymentActivity to build VietQR URLs.

nodes.name: ApiClient
nodes.summary: Singleton class providing a shared Retrofit instance with OkHttp client, Gson converter, and static constants for base URL and bank details.

nodes.name: ApiService.java
nodes.summary: Retrofit service interface defining all 27 backend API endpoints covering authentication, staff management, menu categories, dishes, tables, orders, payments, statistics, and session checking.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Retrofit @interface with annotated method declarations; covers the entire backend API surface including paginated dish listings, CRUD for all entities, and VietQR-based payment flow endpoints.

nodes.name: ApiService
nodes.summary: Retrofit @interface with 27 endpoint methods covering login, staff CRUD, category CRUD, dish CRUD, table CRUD, order lifecycle, payment confirmation, statistics, and session validation.

nodes.name: DisplayCashierFragment.java

nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Handler/Runnable polling loop (startPolling/stopPolling) tied to onResume/onPause lifecycle for efficient background data refresh without a separate service thread.

nodes.name: DisplayCashierFragment
nodes.summary: Fragment providing the cashier view with dual-tab order list (pending/paid), daily revenue totals, and periodic API polling.

nodes.name: loadPendingOrders
nodes.summary: Fetches both pending and paid order lists from the API, parses dates, accumulates revenue totals by payment method, and triggers a UI refresh.

nodes.name: updateRecyclerView
nodes.summary: Switches the RecyclerView adapter data source between pending and paid order lists based on the selected tab, managing empty-state visibility.

nodes.name: DisplayCategoryFragment.java

nodes.name: DisplayCategoryFragment

nodes.name: HienThiDSLoai
nodes.summary: Fetches the list of menu categories from the backend API and populates the adapter, refreshing empty state UI on completion.

nodes.name: DisplayHomeFragment.java
nodes.summary: Home dashboard fragment that displays today's orders and category list via Retrofit API calls, and provides navigation shortcuts to other major sections (statistics, tables, menu, staff) with role-based visibility controlled by SessionManager.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Retrofit callbacks with isAdded() guards to prevent NPEs during fragment lifecycle transitions. Role-based UI visibility is driven by SessionManager.isAdmin().

nodes.name: DisplayHomeFragment
nodes.summary: Fragment class that serves as the home dashboard, loading category and today's order data from the API and handling navigation click events to other fragments.

nodes.name: HienThiDSLoai
nodes.summary: Fetches the menu category list from the API and populates the home screen's horizontal category RecyclerView.

nodes.name: HienThiDonTrongNgay

nodes.name: onClick
nodes.summary: Handles click events on home dashboard quick-access cards, performing fragment transactions to navigate to Statistics, Table, Menu, Staff, or Category screens.

nodes.name: DisplayMenuFragment.java

nodes.languageNotes: Implements pagination via a RecyclerView scroll listener with currentPage/hasMore state, and delegates server-side search by resetting the page and reloading from the API with a query parameter.

nodes.name: DisplayMenuFragment
nodes.summary: Fragment class that provides paginated, searchable menu display for a specific dish category, with admin controls for adding and editing dishes.

nodes.name: taiThemMon
nodes.summary: Loads the next page of dishes from the API for the current category and search query, appending results to the adapter and updating empty state UI.

nodes.name: timKiemTrenServer
nodes.summary: Resets pagination state, sets the current search query string, clears the adapter, and triggers a fresh load from the server for the given search keyword.

nodes.name: capNhatTrangThai
nodes.summary: Toggles visibility of the dish list and empty state layout based on whether the current dish list is empty, and sets descriptive empty state text.

nodes.name: DisplayStaffFragment.java
nodes.summary: Fragment that displays the full staff list with long-press context menu for edit/delete actions, making Retrofit API calls to fetch staff and delete via the manageStaff endpoint, with an options menu for adding new staff (admin-only).

nodes.name: DisplayStaffFragment
nodes.summary: Fragment class that shows the staff list, supports item long-press for context menus, and provides toolbar actions for adding staff with role-gated visibility.

nodes.name: HienThiDSNV
nodes.summary: Fetches the full staff list from the API and populates the RecyclerView adapter, then calls capNhatTrangThai to update empty state visibility.

nodes.name: xoaNhanVien
nodes.summary: Shows a confirmation dialog before calling the API delete endpoint for a staff member, removes the item from the adapter list on success, and shows error toasts on failure.

nodes.name: DisplayStatisticFragment.java
nodes.summary: Fragment that renders revenue statistics with ChipGroup date filters (today/7 days/30 days/all) and an MPAndroidChart bar chart showing daily revenue; loads all paid orders from the API and calculates totals, order count, and average per filter.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses MPAndroidChart BarChart with a custom ValueFormatter that formats revenue values into 'K' (thousands) or 'tr' (millions) suffixes to prevent label overlap, and LinkedHashMap to maintain date ordering.

nodes.name: DisplayStatisticFragment
nodes.summary: Fragment class that provides the revenue statistics dashboard with date-range filtering, summary metrics, order list, and bar chart visualization.

nodes.name: HienThiDSThongKe
nodes.summary: Fetches all paid orders from the API, normalizes date strings, and stores the full dataset in tatCaDonDat before calling capNhatDashboard to update the UI.

nodes.name: capNhatDashboard
nodes.summary: Applies the current date filter to the full order list, computes total revenue, order count and average, updates the summary TextViews, refreshes the RecyclerView adapter, and triggers setupBarChart.

nodes.name: setupBarChart
nodes.summary: Builds and configures the MPAndroidChart BarChart from the filtered order list: groups revenue by date, limits visible bars, applies axis formatting with abbreviated value labels, and animates the chart.
nodes.languageNotes: Limits displayed bars to max(keys.size, 10) to keep the chart readable, and fills in zero-revenue days for continuous date-range displays.

nodes.name: DisplayTableFragment.java
nodes.summary: Fragment that displays the restaurant table grid in a 3-column GridLayout, fetches table status from the API on resume, and provides admin-gated add-table functionality via FAB and options menu.

nodes.name: DisplayTableFragment
nodes.summary: Fragment class that renders restaurant tables in a grid, refreshes table status on fragment resume, and supports table creation for admin users.

nodes.name: HienThiDSBan
nodes.summary: Fetches the table list from the API and populates the grid adapter, then updates empty state visibility.

nodes.name: ReceiptHelper.java
nodes.summary: Utility class providing static helpers for capturing a View as a Bitmap, saving it to the device gallery (with API level branching between MediaStore and legacy file paths), and sharing it via an Intent chooser.
nodes.languageNotes: Branches on Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.Q to use MediaStore ContentResolver on Android 10+ versus legacy Environment.getExternalStoragePublicDirectory on older versions.

nodes.name: ReceiptHelper
nodes.summary: Static utility class for receipt image operations: view capture, gallery save, and sharing.

nodes.name: saveBitmapToGallery
nodes.summary: Saves a receipt Bitmap to the device's public Pictures directory, using MediaStore on API 29+ or direct file I/O on older devices, and broadcasts a media scan intent for legacy paths.

nodes.name: shareBitmap
nodes.summary: Saves the receipt bitmap to the gallery and launches an Android share sheet so the user can send the receipt image via any installed sharing app.

nodes.name: SessionManager.java
nodes.summary: Singleton-style utility class backed by Android SharedPreferences that stores and retrieves the logged-in user's session data (role, staff ID, name, JWT token) and exposes role-check helpers isAdmin() and isCashier().
nodes.languageNotes: All methods are static and accept a Context parameter for SharedPreferences access, making the class stateless and thread-safe for reading.

nodes.name: SessionManager
nodes.summary: Static session management class that wraps Android SharedPreferences to persist user authentication state and expose role-check helpers for admin/cashier access control.

nodes.name: saveSession
nodes.summary: Persists user session data (role, staff ID, full name, and optional JWT token) to SharedPreferences in a single atomic commit.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README describes Royal Restaurant POS as a dual-component system: an Android app for staff ordering and table management, and a web admin portal for cashier and reporting functions. All data is processed centrally on a Cloud VPS running PHP/MySQL behind Cloudflare SSL, with the Android client communicating exclusively through Retrofit REST calls. Reading this document first establishes the system's two-actor model — staff and cashier — which shapes every architectural decision you will encounter in subsequent steps.

tour.title: Build Configuration
tour.description: The app-level build.gradle declares the project's external dependencies and SDK targets. It adds Retrofit and OkHttp for REST communication, Glide for image loading, MPAndroidChart for revenue charts, and the Material Components library for UI styling — exactly the toolkit described in the README. Reviewing this file before reading any Java code tells you which third-party libraries you will encounter and what minimum Android API level (21) the app targets.
tour.languageLesson: Android Gradle build files separate the module-level build.gradle (app-specific dependencies, applicationId, SDK versions) from the project-level build.gradle (repository sources, classpath plugins). The 'implementation' keyword adds a runtime-only dependency; 'testImplementation' scopes it to unit tests only.

tour.title: App Entry Point & Manifest
tour.description: The AndroidManifest.xml registers every Activity in the app and declares the INTERNET, CAMERA, and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permissions required at runtime. It designates SplashActivity as the LAUNCHER, making it the first screen the OS starts. SplashActivity itself is minimal: it plays a logo fade-in animation and then redirects to WelcomeActivity after a timed delay, serving purely as a branded loading screen.
tour.languageLesson: Every Activity, Service, and BroadcastReceiver used by an Android app must be declared in AndroidManifest.xml before the OS can start it. The LAUNCHER/MAIN intent filter on SplashActivity is what causes it to appear in the device's app drawer and be the process entry point.

tour.title: Authentication Flow
tour.description: WelcomeActivity is the first interactive screen: it checks SharedPreferences via SessionManager and auto-redirects authenticated users directly to HomeActivity, bypassing login entirely. For new sessions, LoginActivity sends credentials to the backend API, receives a StaffResponse containing a session token and role, and persists these through SessionManager. The two-step RegisterActivity / Register2ndActivity flow handles self-registration by collecting and validating all required fields before calling the addStaff API endpoint.
tour.languageLesson: SessionManager uses Android SharedPreferences as a lightweight key-value store for persisting session data across app restarts. All methods are static and accept a Context parameter, which keeps the class stateless and avoids a singleton with a retained Application reference — a common source of memory leaks.

tour.title: Main Navigation Hub
tour.description: HomeActivity is the architectural center of the app, confirmed by the highest fan-in score (12 incoming edges) among all Activities. It hosts a NavigationDrawer that swaps between six Fragments: Home, Cashier, Statistic, Table, Category, and Staff. It also enforces role-based menu item visibility — admin users see management screens, cashiers see only the cashier tab — by reading SessionManager at startup. A Handler-based polling loop running on onResume/onPause checks the backend session endpoint to kick out accounts that have been logged in on another device, implementing the single-session constraint.
tour.languageLesson: Android's DrawerLayout + NavigationView pattern is the standard way to implement side navigation drawers. Fragment transactions replace the content area without recreating the host Activity, preserving back-stack state. The Handler.postDelayed polling pattern is a lightweight alternative to WorkManager or JobScheduler for short-interval background checks.

tour.title: Home Dashboard Fragment
tour.description: DisplayHomeFragment is the default fragment shown after login, with the highest fan-out (17) of any file in the project. It loads today's completed orders and the category list from the API, and provides quick-access cards that navigate to every other major section. Role-based visibility hides admin-only cards for cashier accounts by calling SessionManager.isAdmin(). This fragment acts as the operational dashboard the README describes, surfacing the day's activity at a glance.

tour.title: Table Grid & POS Ordering Start
tour.description: DisplayTableFragment renders all restaurant tables in a 3-column grid and refreshes table occupancy status every time the fragment resumes. AdapterDisplayTable is the most complex adapter in the project: when a staff member taps an occupied table, it makes an API call to retrieve the existing order and navigates to an order detail view; tapping an empty table opens the category/menu flow to start a new order. DisplayCategoryFragment and DisplayMenuFragment extend this flow — the staff selects a category, browses a paginated and searchable dish list, then taps a dish to proceed to quantity entry.
tour.languageLesson: Android RecyclerView adapters should ideally be dumb view binders, but in this codebase AdapterDisplayTable embeds Retrofit API calls directly inside onBindViewHolder. This is a deliberate trade-off for simplicity in a small-team project, but in larger apps the API call would be lifted into a ViewModel to avoid triggering network requests on every rebind.

tour.title: Order Creation & Payment Flow
tour.description: AmountMenuActivity validates the requested dish quantity, then either retrieves an existing open order for the table or creates a new one via the API, and appends the line item using the addOrderDetail endpoint. PaymentActivity closes the loop: it displays all ordered items, presents a payment method dialog (cash or VietQR bank-transfer QR code), calls the checkout API, and then polls checkOrderStatus at regular intervals until the cashier confirms payment. On confirmation, it renders a shareable receipt dialog using ReceiptHelper.
tour.languageLesson: PaymentActivity uses Handler.postDelayed to implement a polling loop that checks payment status every few seconds. The loop is started in onResume and cancelled in onDestroy via stopPolling(), ensuring no callbacks fire after the Activity is destroyed. This avoids WebSockets while achieving near-real-time status updates without a persistent connection.

tour.title: API Communication Layer
tour.description: ApiClient is a singleton Retrofit factory (fan-in: 35, the most widely depended-upon class in the project) that configures OkHttp with 30-second timeouts and lenient GSON parsing, and exposes the backend base URL plus VietQR banking constants. ApiService is the Retrofit interface defining all 27 REST endpoints — login, staff CRUD, category CRUD, dish CRUD, table CRUD, order lifecycle, payment confirmation, statistics, and session validation. Every screen in the app obtains its HTTP client via ApiClient.getApiService() and calls one of these annotated methods.
tour.languageLesson: Retrofit interfaces use Java annotations (@GET, @POST, @PUT, @DELETE) and @Path / @Field / @Body parameters to declare HTTP endpoints as pure method signatures. At runtime, Retrofit generates a proxy implementation. The singleton pattern in ApiClient ensures a single OkHttp connection pool is shared across the entire app, avoiding resource exhaustion from multiple client instances.

tour.title: Data Models: DTOs & Response Classes
tour.description: The project maintains two parallel model hierarchies: DTO classes in the DTO package hold in-memory data used by adapters and fragments, while Response classes in the Api package are GSON-deserialized directly from JSON. MonDTO carries a menu item including both a byte-array and a URL path for its image; DonDatDTO is the core order record used by cashier and statistics screens; ThanhToanDTO binds payment line items to the receipt adapter. OrderResponse has the highest fan-in of any model (19), appearing in every screen that reads or processes an order.
tour.languageLesson: Separating Response POJOs (deserialized from JSON) from DTO classes (used by the UI layer) is a clean-architecture principle: it insulates the UI from backend contract changes. When the server renames a field, only the Response class and a mapping step need to change, not all the adapters.

tour.title: Cashier Dashboard
tour.description: DisplayCashierFragment is the screen described in the README's cashier role section. It polls the API on a Handler loop (startPolling/stopPolling tied to onResume/onPause) to display a live tab-switched list of pending and paid orders, alongside today's cash and bank-transfer revenue totals. When a cashier selects a pending order, CashierConfirmActivity loads the order's line items into a RecyclerView and presents cash or bank-transfer confirmation buttons that call the payment confirmation API endpoint.

tour.title: Statistics & Reporting
tour.description: DisplayStatisticFragment provides the revenue analytics view described in the README. It fetches all paid orders, applies a ChipGroup date filter (today / last 7 days / last 30 days / all time), computes total revenue, order count, and average order value, and renders an MPAndroidChart bar chart with per-day revenue grouped by date. Tapping any bar or order row opens DetailStatisticActivity, which shows the full line-item breakdown for that order using the getOrderDetails API endpoint.
tour.languageLesson: MPAndroidChart's BarChart requires a BarDataSet built from BarEntry objects where the x-axis is a float index rather than a date string. A custom ValueFormatter is attached to the axis to convert those float indices back to human-readable labels. Bar values are abbreviated (K for thousands, 'tr' for millions) to prevent label overlap on narrow screens.

tour.title: Receipt Helper Utility
tour.description: ReceiptHelper is a static utility class that sits at the deepest point of the BFS traversal (depth 4 from HomeActivity), meaning it is a pure leaf — nothing depends on it except PaymentActivity. It provides three operations: capturing a View hierarchy as a Bitmap, saving that Bitmap to the device gallery (using MediaStore on Android 10+ or legacy file I/O on older devices), and launching the system share sheet. This is how customers receive their receipt image after payment is confirmed.
tour.languageLesson: Android's scoped storage model (API 29+) requires apps to insert files into the MediaStore rather than writing directly to external storage paths. ReceiptHelper branches on Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.Q to use the correct API, illustrating the backward-compatibility pattern common in Android utilities that need to support a wide API range.

tour.title: Admin Management Screens
tour.description: The staff, category, and dish management screens follow a consistent pattern: a Fragment shows a RecyclerView list backed by an API call, and tapping add or edit launches a dedicated Activity that validates all fields before calling the create or update endpoint. AddStaffActivity performs the most thorough validation in the project — 8 separate methods covering name, username, email, phone, password regex, gender, role, and minimum age. AddCategoryActivity and AddMenuActivity additionally handle image selection, bitmap resizing, and Base64 encoding before submitting to the backend.
tour.languageLesson: Android's ActivityResultLauncher API (replacing the deprecated startActivityForResult) registers a contract before the Activity is created, receives the result asynchronously, and avoids the request-code integer juggling of the old pattern. DisplayCategoryFragment uses this to refresh its list after AddCategoryActivity finishes.

tour.title: UI Resources & Design System
tour.description: The res/ directory contains the visual language of the entire app. Shape drawables (corner_border_black, corner_border_primary, circle_drawable) provide rounded input fields and status indicators without custom Views. The six slide and fade animation XMLs define all screen transition effects. The layout files follow a consistent structure: a full-screen RecyclerView for list screens, a scrollable card form for add/edit screens, and a compact dialog layout for quantity entry and table creation. The reusable layout_empty_state.xml is shared across every list screen to display a consistent "no items" message.
tour.languageLesson: Android shape drawables defined in XML (GradientDrawable) are a zero-overhead alternative to bitmap assets for simple UI shapes like rounded rectangles and circles. They scale perfectly on all screen densities and can be tinted programmatically at runtime, making them the preferred approach for dynamic status indicators such as the table occupancy badges in this app.
